Examples of my confusion:

I saw these and they look like what I want. I think the same guy is selling this, but it costs 3 times as much and has fewer speakers. Which I don't understand. Can someone explain this?

Now this guy has a ton of stuff he's selling. These look the best to me, but obviously they're not since they're only $30. I was thinking, well maybe they're just broken, because then he's got these for $90 in "excellent" condition. But these dumb looking ones are $400?!
I'm a noob who needs help looking at deals on craigslist.

i dont know much, but this should get you started:

with speakers and amplifiers, you want to make sure your amp doesnt put out more power than the speakers are capable of.

a 300w amp, over 2 channels (left and right) will put 150w maximum to each channel

^dont hook up that amplifier to a set of speakers capable of handling 100w max.

RMS power is the "constant" power it sends to each speaker, and will be less than peak power. (higher RMS power means better general sound in my opinion.)

secondly, you must match the impedance (resistance) of the speakers to the amp. a higher impedance speaker is not going to hurt your amp (if amp rated at 4ohm capable, and you put 8ohm speakers, no problem... you just wont have as much power going to the speakers as you would with 4ohm)

a LOWER impedance than your amp is capable of, that's how you blow up amplifiers. possibly speakers too, but not sure on that one. (running a 2ohm speaker on a 4ohm-stable amp will let too much current out, and it'll fry the amp)

lastly, i'd generally recommend taking off any speaker grilles/covers and look at the speaker itself.... make sure the rubber/butyl/foam surrounding the speaker is intact. I'd also ask them if they have a way to demo the speakers before you buy. i think a speaker can still be blown/sound like shit, even though you cant look at it and see any deformity.

that's my limited knowledge on the issue; hope it helps
